author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: A French AI lab that publishes many of its models openly.
what_it_does: Mistral trains large models and releases a substantial portion of them under open licences, so anyone can download and run them. It sells hosted access and enterprise deployments on top. It is Europe's leading frontier-scale lab.
how_it_makes_money: Paid hosted access, enterprise licensing, and on-premises deployments for customers who need data to stay inside their own systems.
why_it_matters: It is the main test of whether an open-weight strategy can support a frontier-scale business, and Europe's principal claim to AI sovereignty.
competitive_position: Competes with American labs on quality and with other open-weight providers on price. European government and defence preference for a local supplier is a real advantage.
key_risks: Giving models away limits how much can be charged for them.
Far less capital than American rivals, against a cost curve that keeps rising.
Open weights are copied instantly by competitors.
Its regional advantage does not travel outside Europe.

glossary.definition: The trained model file is published, so anyone can run or adapt it themselves rather than paying for access.
Software running on the customer's own machines rather than the vendor's, usually for privacy or regulatory reasons.
